lem-framed-link-diagram-calculus:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal A$ be a smooth planar
annulus and let $X=\mathcal A\times(-1,1)$, the interior of a solid torus.
A regular annular diagram is a finite immersed union of circles in
$\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)$ with only finitely many transverse double
points, no triple points, and over/under data from the interval coordinate.
The **blackboard framing** is the normal strip lying in the annulus. A specified
framing differs from it on each component by an integer full-twist correction,
measured by the winding number of its normal direction relative to the
blackboard normal. Count the correction positively for an A-type full twist,
whose local curl has A-smoothing equal to the straight strip with one
contractible circle; count the opposite B-type twist negatively. Every framed
link in $X$ admits a regular annular diagram. The correction may be recorded
as signed full-twist marks on diagram arcs; its total is additive when arcs
are concatenated.

If two framed links in $X$ are ambient isotopic through links in $X$, their
regular annular diagrams are related by finitely many annular planar isotopies
and local oriented Reidemeister I, II, and III moves in disks contained in
$\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)$. Reidemeister II and III and planar isotopy
preserve the blackboard framing; an A-type or B-type Reidemeister I move
changes it by one corresponding full twist, so the correction integer changes
by the opposite twist. For framed links in $S^3$, every link also admits a
regular planar diagram, and any two diagrams of ambient-isotopic framed links
are related by a finite planar-isotopy/Reidemeister sequence with the same
framing-correction rule.
lem-kauffman-bracket-module-framing-twis:
## Statement

Let $M$ be a smooth oriented $3$-manifold and let $L$ be a framed unoriented
link in its interior with a specified component. A positive full framing twist is the local blackboard
curl whose $A$-smoothing is the straight strip with one additional
zero-framed trivial circle; a negative full framing twist is the curl whose
$B$-smoothing is the straight strip with one additional zero-framed trivial
circle. Write $L^+$ and $L^-$ for the links obtained by inserting these twists
on one component. With $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$ and
$\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$, the module classes satisfy
$$
[L^+]=-A^3[L],\qquad [L^-]=-A^{-3}[L].
$$
lem-general-3manifold-skein-quotient-iso:
## Statement

Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth oriented $3$-manifolds, and let
$f:M\to N$ be an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism. Then
$[L]\mapsto[f(L)]$ induces an $R$-module isomorphism
$f_*:\mathcal K_A(M)\to\mathcal K_A(N)$. These maps respect identity
diffeomorphisms and composition.

Let $\Sigma$ be a compact oriented surface with a specified product collar
$\iota:\Sigma\times[0,1]\hookrightarrow M$ whose lower face lies in
$\partial M$. The stacking product on
$\mathcal K_A(\Sigma\times[0,1])$ and collar gluing define a unital left
action on $\mathcal K_A(M)$: a closed framed link in the surface product is
placed in a sufficiently thin outer subcollar and united with a framed link
in the interior of $M$. The action is independent of the thin-collar width,
associative, and natural under orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms that
respect the specified collars. Only closed framed links are glued; no relative
boundary endpoints are part of this action.
lem-kauffman-bracket-evaluation-is-invar:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and let $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$ and
$\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. For a nonempty framed unoriented link $L$ in $S^3$,
choose a regular planar diagram $D$ of its core. Let $m_j\in\mathbb Z$ be
the full-twist correction on the $j$th component from the blackboard framing
of $D$ to the specified framing of $L$, counting an A-type twist positively
and its inverse negatively as in the framed diagram calculus, and put
$m=\sum_jm_j$. For a state
$S$ of $D$, let $a(S)$ and $b(S)$ be its numbers of A- and B-smoothings and
$|S|$ its number of resulting circles. The assignment
$$
E(\varnothing)=1,\qquad
E(L)=\delta(-A^3)^m\sum_{S}A^{a(S)-b(S)}\delta^{|S|-1}
$$
is independent of the diagram and twist corrections and extends
$R$-linearly to a map $E:\mathcal K_A(S^3)\to R$ satisfying
$E([\varnothing])=1$.
lem-annular-kauffman-bracket-state-expan:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal A$ be a planar annulus
and identify the solid torus with $\mathcal A\times[-1,1]$. Let
$R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$, $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$, and let $z$ be a formal
polynomial variable. For a regular annular diagram $D$, a state $S$ smooths
every crossing. Let $a(S)$ and $b(S)$ count its A- and B-smoothings, let
$u(S)$ count the resulting circles that bound disks in $\mathcal A$, and let
$e(S)$ count the resulting circles that do not bound disks in $\mathcal A$;
call a circle that does not bound a disk essential.
If $m$ is the total full-twist correction from the blackboard framing to the
specified framing, counting an A-type twist positively and its inverse
negatively as in the framed diagram calculus, set
$$
\Psi(D,m)=(-A^3)^m\sum_S A^{a(S)-b(S)}\delta^{u(S)}z^{e(S)}.
$$
This value is independent of the regular annular diagram and twist correction
of the framed link and induces an $R$-linear map
$$
\Psi:\mathcal K_A(\mathcal A\times[-1,1])\longrightarrow R[z].
$$
For the empty link, the empty diagram has its unique empty state and the
formula gives $\Psi(\varnothing)=1$.

The diagram below shows one essential core curve and one contractible circle
in an annular state; every smoothed component is classified by these two
types.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.75,line cap=round]
  \draw[thick] (0,0) circle (1.6);
  \draw[thick] (0,0) circle (0.65);
  \draw[very thick] (0,0) circle (1.05);
  \draw[very thick] (1.30,0) circle (0.16);
  \node at (0,1.05) [above] {$z$};
  \node at (1.45,0.25) [right] {$\bigcirc$};
  \node at (0,-1.95) {essential core and contractible circle};
\end{tikzpicture}
```
thm-skein-module-of-s-three-is-rank-one:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and let $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$ and
$\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. The Kauffman bracket skein module
$\mathcal K_A(S^3)$ is freely generated as an $R$-module by the empty link.
In particular, a zero-framed trivial circle represents
$\delta[\varnothing]$.
thm-skein-module-of-solid-torus-has-core:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and let $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$. Identify
the solid torus with $\mathcal A\times[-1,1]$, where $\mathcal A$ is a planar
annulus. A simple closed curve is called essential if it does not bound a disk
in $\mathcal A$. Every framed link in this product admits a regular annular
diagram and an integer framing correction from its blackboard framing. Let
$z$ be one blackboard-framed annular core curve, and for $n\geq1$ let $z^n$
denote $n$ parallel copies of that curve, with $z^0$ the empty link. In the polynomial
ring $R[z]$, $z$ is also the formal variable sent to the core class $[z]$.
Then the classes $[z^n]$, $n\geq0$, form an $R$-basis of
$\mathcal K_A(\mathcal A\times[-1,1])$. Equivalently, the map
$J:R[z]\to\mathcal K_A(\mathcal A\times[-1,1])$ sending $z^n$ to $[z^n]$ is
an $R$-module isomorphism.
lem-skein-module-isomorphism-respects-fr:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. An orientation-preserving diffeomorphism
between smooth oriented $3$-manifolds transports the full framing of every
link and induces an isomorphism of their Kauffman bracket skein modules. If
the diffeomorphism carries a specified product collar of a compact oriented
boundary surface productwise to another specified collar, the induced
isomorphism intertwines the two closed-link collar actions. A positive or
negative full framing twist on one link component multiplies its class by
$-A^3$ or $-A^{-3}$, respectively. In $\mathcal K_A(S^3)$, a positive twist
of a zero-framed trivial circle changes its class from
$\delta[\varnothing]$ to $-A^3\delta[\varnothing]$, with
$\delta[\varnothing]\ne -A^3\delta[\varnothing]$. In the solid-torus
module, a positive twist of the blackboard-framed core changes $[z]$ to
$-A^3[z]$, with $[z]\ne -A^3[z]$.
